submitted.rationale: Of the three measured samples, idx 14 (Mg0.80Mn0.20) had the highest photocurrent at 7e-8 A. This is the Mg-rich regime of Mn in a MgO-type host with Mg3MnO4-like phases (predicted HSE gap 2.24 eV, which absorbs at 3.22 eV).

rejected.reason: The MgMn2O4 spinel composition gave a measured photocurrent of 0, even though it is predicted stable and absorbing.
The Mn-rich end gave only 1e-8 A; its small-gap Mn-rich phases (about 1 eV) probably suffer heavy recombination.

consultations.verdict: Support: MgMn2O4 spinel (mp-27510) is on the MACE hull and has HSE gap 2.87 eV < 3.22 eV photon energy, so it absorbs; Mg6MnO8 gap 3.74 eV would not absorb. Index 12 (Mg 0.333) is exactly spinel stoichiometry.

Weak support: the spinel composition (idx 12) gave zero. Mg-rich phases such as Mg3MnO4 (HSE gap 2.24 eV) absorb at 3.22 eV and form a distinct regime (Mn in a MgO-type host). Mn3O4 (0.94 eV) at the Mn-rich end is likely too small-gap and metallic-like for photocurrent. Idx 14 is the Mg-rich extreme and the GP maximum-uncertainty pick.

Uninformative to mildly against: MgMn5O8 has a predicted gap of 1.21 eV, so it absorbs strongly but may recombine heavily. Idx 14 is already the most Mg-rich sample, so the only unexplored regime is the Mn-rich end. I'm measuring idx 2 for coverage.
